headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: Recovery holding, but the mood is mixed this week

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The longer-term picture has improved enough to support spending more on acquiring new users, especially for products aimed at active traders rather than stablecoin savers. Because the 200-day average has not turned up yet and this week's mood is mixed, scale up in steps rather than all at once, and keep some budget flexible so it can be pulled back if price falls back below its long-term average. This describes today's conditions, not a forecast.

reasons: BTC is about 20% above its 200-day average.
Price is up about 38% over the last 90 days.
The 200-day average is still sloping down (-4% over 90 days): early recovery, not confirmed.
Still about 31% below the all-time high, leaving room before the market looks overheated.
watch: The headline mood says greed, but more traders are paying to bet on a fall than a rise. If price keeps holding up, those bets can unwind and add fuel; if price slips, the cheerful mood can sour quickly.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger picture still points up, but this week is a coin flip. Short term, the mood is balanced: the Fear & Greed index reads a greedy 73, yet in the futures market more people are now paying to bet on a fall than on a rise. That split usually means nervous, choppy days rather than a clear direction; a calmer, one-sided mood would firm it up, and big promotions may land better once things settle.

Over the next month, the picture leans moderately positive. Price is up about 38% over the last 90 days, but only about half of those days finished above the long-term average, so much of the gain came from a recent push rather than steady climbing. The US spot Bitcoin funds also saw about $85M leave on the latest day, and the next Fed rate decision is on 27 October; steady money coming back into those funds would strengthen this lean, more outflows would weaken it.

Over the next 3-6 months, the trend leans positive but is still young. Price sits about 20% above its 200-day average, yet that average itself is still sloping down, which is what an early recovery looks like rather than a confirmed long uptrend. Price is also still about 31% below its all-time high (see the levels below); the 200-day average turning upward would confirm it, a fall back under it would undo it.

team_notes.marketing: Lean into active-trader and non-stablecoin channels, leading with the real story of a roughly 38% recovery over three months rather than urgency or fear-of-missing-out. The mood index is already greedy at 73 while many traders are betting on a fall, so avoid hype-heavy creative this week and keep stablecoin and savings messaging running as a steady base.
